title: Building a Secure Power Platform Architecture with Managed Identity and VNet
summary: Remove secrets and public paths: managed identity (no secret to steal) and VNet injection (no public path) for Dataverse plug-ins.
whyItMatters: Two architecture holes become two manageable operational concerns.

keyPoints.heading: The problem
keyPoints.text: Every integration must answer who's calling and where traffic goes; common secret-hiding approaches are obfuscation.

keyPoints.heading: Managed identity
keyPoints.text: Entra workload identity with federated identity credential and short-lived tokens; user-assigned MI default; Key Vault Secrets User role; FIC tied to environment ID and plug-in cert hash; pac managed-identity (preview).

keyPoints.heading: ALM tips
keyPoints.text: Pre-pick MI GUID across environments; sign assemblies (CA cert in prod); keep certs in Key Vault/GitHub env secrets; timestamp signatures.

keyPoints.heading: VNet
keyPoints.text: Delegate a subnet; NSG is the boundary (deny internet, allow VirtualNetwork); two VNets in paired regions required; pre-provision (30-60 min recycle); private endpoints and DNS; fail fast to avoid 2-minute timeout.

keyPoints.heading: Not covered by VNet
keyPoints.text: Governance (Managed Environments, DLP) and observability (NSG flow logs, App Insights).
